cases.expected: The method returns the same long[2] array as MurmurHash3.hash128x64(data, 0, data.length, 0).
cases.description: Typical non‑empty input – verifies that the one‑argument overload forwards the call correctly with offset 0, length =data.length and seed 0 and returns the exact same 128‑bit hash.

cases.expected: The method returns the same long[2] array as MurmurHash3.hash128x64(data, 0, 0, 0) (i.e. the hash of an empty array).
cases.description: Empty array – checks that the overload works for length 0 and that the delegation does not throw or alter the result.
Null input – the one‑argument overload should immediately throw NPE because it tries to read data.length.

cases.expected: The method returns the same long[2] array as MurmurHash3.hash128x64(data, 0, 1024, 0).
cases.description: Large input (1 KB) – ensures that the delegation works for bigger payloads and does not hit any hidden length‑related branches.

cases.expected: Returns a long[2] array equal to MurmurHash3.hash128x64(data, 0, 1, 0).
cases.description: Single‑byte input – checks that the one‑argument overload correctly forwards a length of 1 and produces the same 128‑bit hash as the four‑argument version.

cases.expected: Returns a long[2] array equal to MurmurHash3.hash128x64(data, 0, 16, 0).
cases.description: Exactly one 16‑byte block – verifies correct handling of a full block boundary.

cases.expected: Returns a long[2] array equal to MurmurHash3.hash128x64(data, 0, 15, 0).
cases.description: Fifteen bytes (one byte short of a full block) – ensures the tail‑processing path yields the same result as the four‑argument overload.

cases.expected: Returns a long[2] array equal to MurmurHash3.hash128x64(data, 0, 17, 0).
cases.description: Seventeen bytes (one byte over a full block) – tests the algorithm’s handling of a second, incomplete block.

cases.expected: Returns a long[2] array equal to MurmurHash3.hash128x64(data, 0, 4, 0).
cases.description: Array containing negative‑valued bytes (signed byte values) – confirms that the hash treats byte values as unsigned 8‑bit data.

cases.expected: Two successive calls return different long[2] object references (but equal contents).
cases.description: Object‑identity test – ensures the method creates a fresh result array each time rather than reusing a static buffer.

cases.expected: The hash value returned before mutating the array remains equal to MurmurHash3.hash128x64(original, 0, original.length, 0) after the array is changed.
cases.description: Immutability test – verifies that the computed hash is not affected by later modifications to the original byte array.
